data.narrative:
Atomic Machines is a Series A chip-design company founded by Jeff Holden that has raised $144M to date. The valuation universe consists of 11 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors plus 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD). Notable private peers include SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

Stage-progression methodology was the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $144M as a proxy for implied pre-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement yields an implied post-valuation of $288M. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient comparable density within narrow stage and tier filters—while 11 same-sector peers exist, none of the filtered subsets met the minimum threshold of three datapoints necessary to establish a reliable median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $245M (low) to $331M (high), with a median of $288M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct comparable valuation data from same-stage peers, reliance on a single quantitative method, and lack of visibility into Atomic Machines' revenue, burn rate, or technical validation metrics. Any refinement would require additional comparable data or direct market benchmarking against identified peers.
